children: , the power-generation and grid-equipment company, ended its commercial dispute with Vineyard Wind after withdrawing its termination notice and pending appeal. Shares gained approximately 2.3% to $946.45 on Thursday morning, putting the focus back on execution rather than the courtroom.

The fight centered on GE Vernova's $1.3 billion contract tied to the $4.5 billion offshore-wind project. Reuters previously reported that GE claimed roughly $360 million remained unpaid before a judge ordered the company to continue its work. That figure represented about 27.7% of the reported contract value. The legal overhang has now eased, but the economics are still murky because the settlement terms remain confidential. Investors do not yet know how much cash GE recovered, whether claims were reduced, or what concessions may have been exchanged.

Vineyard Wind says all turbines are now capable of generating electricity and the project can supply more than 400,000 homes and businesses, preserving an important construction and service relationship for GE Vernova. The GuruFocus picture adds a sharp counterweight to the upbeat operational news: GE Vernova carries a GF Score of just 15 out of 100, with Financial Strength standing out as its relatively strongest displayed factor while profitability remains weak and the other categories show little support. In other words, settling the dispute removes one uncertainty, but the valuation and fundamental profile still give investors plenty to examine beyond Thursday's share-price gain.

title: GE Vernova Gains 2.3% as $1.3 Billion Wind Fight Ends
